title: Why automatic saving beats good intentions

scenes.say: You meant to save. The default decided.
Some employers make you sign up for retirement savings. Others enroll you automatically, and you can opt out anytime.
Same choice. Same freedom. Only the starting point changes.
When one large US company switched to automatic enrollment, participation jumped by about forty-eight percentage points.
Present bias makes us delay. A default removes the decision. So doing nothing becomes saving.
So what if saving happened before you could decide? An automatic transfer on payday does exactly that.
